title: Lost
Creek
thesis: Granite domes and a creek that disappears underground, two hours from the cheapest airport in the West. Below treeline nearly the whole way, which is the point in storm season. Josh — August 17 to 19, 2026.

profile.note: Trailhead and Wigwam Park are USGS 10-metre DEM values at surveyed coordinates; the line between them is drawn straight because no source gives the intermediate profile. The real trail undulates — Hiking Project logs a 10,120-foot high point and 2,377 feet of gain over the full length, more than the endpoints suggest.

why: Lost Creek is the cheapest way out of Austin into real wilderness. Denver fares run $247 nonstop on Southwest, the cheapest cars on that lot quote under a hundred dollars for three days, and the trailhead is two hours from the terminal. Solo, where nothing splits, those two lines are the difference between a five-hundred-dollar trip and an eight-hundred-dollar one. The schedule cooperates too: a 6:55 AM flight out and a 7:55 PM flight home on day three, so neither end needs a motel.

It also happens to be the right shape for August. This is a wilderness of Pikes Peak granite domes and hoodoos with the trail threading below them at eight to nine thousand feet — under treeline nearly the whole way, in a month when the high country gets hit by lightning most afternoons. Lost Creek itself vanishes into and out of the rock repeatedly, which is the thing people come to see. Water is reliable, camps are established, and the trail is popular enough to be a solo-friendly place to be alone.

days.title: Fly in, walk up the creek
log: US-285 southwest to Pine Junction, about 20 miles
South on CR-126 about 22 miles, then FR-211 (Matukat Road) west 11 miles — gravel, ordinary-car passable when dry
Goose Creek trailhead, 7,709 ft. Fill out the free wilderness permit at the board — it's mandatory here
Camp up the Goose Creek valley, roughly 4–5 miles in, 100 ft off the creek and the trail
notes: Legal sites are genuinely scarce in the lower valley — the Forest Service says so plainly, because the setback is 100 feet from both water and trail and the canyon is tight. Start walking early enough to be choosy, and be willing to go further than planned to camp legally.

days.title: The Shafthouse, the domes, the sinks
notes: The day this trip exists for, walked with a light pack. The Shafthouse sits 3.8 miles from the trailhead — the surviving bunkhouses and shaft works of the Antero and Lost Park Reservoir Company's attempt, in the 1890s, to dam a creek that kept vanishing into the granite. The scheme failed; the buildings are still standing.

Above it, Refrigerator Gulch and the sinks where Lost Creek disappears under the rock and re-emerges, with red granite domes over the whole thing. Wander as far as the weather and the legs allow, then back to camp.

days.title: Out and home the same day
notes: Downhill and easy. The 7:55 PM departure leaves about seven hours of slack after reaching the car — more than any single thing that can go wrong on eleven miles of gravel road. If that wait is too long, Southwest also flies at 3:50 PM and 12:50 PM, and Frontier at 4:14 PM; all were confirmed nonstop for this date.

map.intro: The first decision is at the trailhead itself, where two trails leave together. After that the valley does the navigating for you — which is a large part of why this works alone.

waypoints.name: Denver airport (DEN)
waypoints.popup: Land 8:10 AM. About 2 hours to the trailhead, last 11 miles gravel.

waypoints.name: Goose Creek trailhead
waypoints.popup:
Mile 0 · 7,709 ft
Mandatory free self-issue wilderness permit at the board. Goose Creek #612 and Hankins Pass #630 both start here — take #612, north up the creek.

waypoints.note: Dispersed camping, no fixed site — so no coordinate. Interpolated by trail mile on the diagram only and marked approximate. Legal sites need 100 ft of clearance from both the creek and the trail, and they are scarce down low.

Mile 9.7 · 9,548 ft
North end of Goose Creek #612, at the junction with Wigwam Trail #609. The far turnaround if legs and weather cooperate.

waypoints.name: Hankins Pass (not our route)
waypoints.popup: 10,010 ft · Hankins Pass Trail #630 leaves the same trailhead and climbs southwest. The wrong turn to avoid on day one.

map.drive_note: US-285 southwest from Denver about 20 miles to Pine Junction, south on County Road 126 about 22 miles, then Forest Road 211 (the Matukat Road) west about 11 miles to the campground and trailhead. Roughly two hours. The last 11 miles are unpaved; the Forest Service posts no high-clearance warning, so an ordinary car does it when dry.
map.caveat: The diagram is the offline and print fallback — no network, survives a dead phone. The dashed line is straight-line spacing between surveyed waypoints, not the trail. Camp is a hollow marker because it is interpolated by mileage, not surveyed. The Wigwam Park coordinate is an OpenStreetMap node on Wigwam Creek, not a surveyed park centre — close enough to place the far end of the trail, not a navigation target. Carry the paper sheet.

route.title: Goose Creek trailhead
route.body: End of eleven gravel miles on FR-211, next to Goose Creek Campground. Parking and horse facilities, and a permit board. The self-issue wilderness permit here is mandatory, not courtesy — Lost Creek is one of the few Colorado wildernesses that requires one. It is free. Elevation is the USGS 10-metre DEM value at the Forest Service coordinate; the agency lists the adjacent campground at 7,723 ft, which agrees.

route.title: Goose Creek #612, not Hankins Pass #630
route.body: Two trails leave this trailhead. Take Goose Creek Trail #612, north up the creek. Hankins Pass Trail #630 climbs southwest toward a 10,010-foot pass — a fine trail and entirely the wrong direction for this trip.

route.title: Up the valley, looking for a legal site
route.body: The trail winds north with the creek through Pikes Peak granite. Water throughout. The Forest Service's own warning is worth repeating: the lower valley is tight and good legal campsites are scarce, because the wilderness order requires 100 feet of separation from lakes, streams, and trails alike. Walk until you find one rather than settling for an illegal spot near the water.

photo.commons: Rock Formations Near Summit of Bison Peak in Colorado.jpg
photo.caption: Granite formations in the Lost Creek Wilderness, near the summit of Bison Peak

route.title: The Shafthouse
route.body: A signed spur leads to the standing bunkhouses and the remains of the shaft house — the 1890s works of the Antero and Lost Park Reservoir Company, who tried to dam Lost Creek and discovered that a creek which flows through granite rather than over it cannot be impounded. The most-walked destination in this half of the wilderness, and a reasonable turnaround in itself: about 10.6 miles round trip from the trailhead if you add the creek below the buildings.

route.title: Refrigerator Gulch and the sinks
route.body: Where Lost Creek does the thing it is named for — vanishing into the rock and surfacing again downstream, with domes and hoodoos above. This is the day-two wander, done with a light pack from camp. Distances beyond the Shafthouse are not well sourced; treat the map and the weather as the limit, not a mileage target.

route.title: Wigwam Park, if you go the distance
route.body: Goose Creek #612 ends here at the junction with Wigwam Trail #609 — 9.7 miles from the trailhead, with 2,377 feet of cumulative gain and a 10,120-foot high point along the way. Reaching it and returning makes for a long second day; it is the stretch goal, not the plan.

route.title: The return
route.body: Straight back down the valley to the trailhead — losing what you climbed, on a trail you have already read once. Sign out if there's a register. The gravel road is the last obstacle, and it is easier in daylight going out than it was coming in.

rows.note: Southwest nonstop both ways for these exact dates — out 6:55 AM Aug 17, back 7:55 PM Aug 19. Google Flights, checked 2026-07-28, rated typical pricing.
Southwest charges $45/bag each way on basic fares since April 2026.
Denver is the cheapest rental market of the three: a compact SUV quoted $67 total across Expedia, Kayak and Booking for these dates. Budgeting $90 for fees and a normal car class.
~230 miles round trip from the airport.

rows.item: Fuel canister and odds and ends
rows.note: Bought near Denver — canisters can't fly.
Rope and a dry bag. A hard-sided canister is not required, but a hang to the posted spec is — 10 ft up and 4 ft out, by forest order.
None — morning flight in, night flight out.
Free, but mandatory. Fill it out at the trailhead board.

hazard.title: A tight canyon, a hard rule, and nobody to send
hazard.intro: This is the gentlest of the three options and still not casual alone. Its specific problems are a camping rule that is easy to break, a creek canyon that concentrates weather and water, and the ordinary solo arithmetic of having no second person.
points: 100 feet from water and trail, both. Lost Creek's wilderness order (in force through 2027) sets the setback at 100 feet from lakes, streams and trails for camping, fires, and tethering. Sites meeting it are scarce in the lower canyon — plan to walk past the obvious spots.
Satellite messenger on your body, check-in schedule someone is watching, and the route, camp, plate and walk-out deadline left at home. No signal in the canyon.

Stoves only, and check the order. Stage 2 restrictions covered this district when checked and allow only liquid or gas devices in a three-foot cleared area. The order as written expired August 1 — assume restrictions and verify.

Hang to the posted spec: 10 feet up, 4 feet out. A forest-wide food storage order (in force to 2028) makes this mandatory, not good practice, and it explicitly covers cookware, toothpaste and sunscreen — not just food. And 2026 is a bad bear year: drought and a record-low snowpack failed the berry and acorn crop, statewide bear reports passed 1,100 by mid-June, and Colorado's first bear attack of the year came in June in Jefferson County, on the drive in. Stand your ground in an encounter, make yourself large, and never run.
Storms funnel here. Being below treeline helps with lightning but not with flash runoff in a tight granite canyon. Don't camp in the streambed, however flat and inviting.

Standing dead near the trailhead. The first stretch crosses the 2002 Hayman burn, where snags fall in wind — and a December 2025 windstorm left the district warning of many weakened trees. Don't camp under a dead one, and think twice about lingering there in a blow.
The road is the weak link. Eleven gravel miles in an ordinary rental, no signal, no partner vehicle. Drive it in daylight both ways and don't try it after heavy rain.
hazard.outro: Bring the permit discipline and the campsite discipline and this is about as forgiving as western backpacking gets alone.

weather.intro: Mid-August in the Colorado Front Range high country means clear mornings and afternoon thunderstorms most days, driven by monsoon moisture pushing north. Being below treeline is this route's main defence. These are station normals, not a forecast.
weather.source: Grant, Colorado co-op station normals (8,963 ft by DEM, WRCC, 1963–2013 record) — the nearest mountain station, on US-285 north of the wilderness. Camp is slightly lower than the station, so figures are close to unadjusted; nights on the higher ground run colder. Checked 2026-07-28.

before.p: Plan a stove-only trip and don't plan a campfire at all. Stage 2 restrictions took effect June 30, 2026 across this district — gas or liquid-fuel stoves only, in a three-foot cleared area, no wood or charcoal. The forest order as signed expires August 1 and no successor had been published as of July 29, but Park County's own Stage II ban has no end date, fire danger reads Very High, and Colorado is in its worst drought on record after the lowest snowpack ever recorded. Re-check the forest alerts page within 48 hours of leaving.
Lost Creek requires a mandatory free self-issue wilderness permit, which is unusual for Colorado. Fill it in at the trailhead board — this is the detail most people miss.

Goose Creek runs alongside the trail for most of the route — the wet part of this wilderness. But Colorado rivers were at roughly half of normal flow in late July, so carry more capacity than a normal August and don't count on side trickles. Filter everything; the Forest Service warns all sources here may carry giardia. Goose Creek Campground at the trailhead has a potable hand pump, open through Labor Day weekend — top off there.
The mildest of the three trips: trailhead 7,709 feet and camps around 8,600. Coming from Austin you will still notice it, but this is the option that doesn't punish a same-day arrival.

Eleven miles of unpaved FR-211 (Matukat Road) after 42 miles of pavement. The Forest Service posts no high-clearance requirement, which is why this trip works with the cheapest car on the lot — but it's washboard, and wet weather changes the calculation.

Group limit 15 people (25 combined with pack animals), dogs on a leash, no bicycles or game carts, pack out all refuse, nothing left unattended more than 72 hours. All from the wilderness order in force through December 31, 2027.

booking.title: Flight — $247 Southwest, out 6:55 AM Aug 17, back 7:55 PM Aug 19
booking.body: Southwest, and not the budget carrier on the same route. Frontier flies this nonstop for $118, but it charges separately for carry-on and checked bags at rates published only as date-dependent ranges — and a pack with a stove and poles has to be checked. The real Frontier total can't be pinned down, and by the time it is, the gap has largely closed. Southwest's $45 a bag is a knowable number. Times were read live and repeat daily, but schedules get reshuffled — recheck when booking.

booking.title: The cheapest car at Denver
booking.body: Denver quoted a compact SUV at $67 total for three days across three booking sites — the cheapest car in this whole research effort. Take it; the road wants nothing more.

booking.title: No campsite, no motel
booking.body: Dispersed camping, permit self-issued at the board. Goose Creek Campground next door is first-come only at $27 if plans change.

booking.title: Call the South Platte ranger district — (303) 275-5610
booking.body: This trailhead is South Platte, not South Park — the wilderness spans both. Two questions that actually matter: whether fire restrictions have been re-issued for August, and the current state of FR-211 for a passenger car. Worth also asking about blowdown; a December 2025 windstorm alert for this district warned of many downed and weakened trees, and it has not been rescinded.

South Park Ranger District, Fairplay — the Lost Park side · (719) 836-2031
Recommended map: National Geographic Trails Illustrated #105, Tarryall Mountains / Kenosha Pass
open_questions: Distances beyond the Shafthouse spur (3.8 mi) are not well sourced — Refrigerator Gulch and the sinks are described in trip reports without consistent mileage. Day two is deliberately written as a wander, not a mileage plan.

Hiking Project gives Goose Creek #612 a 8,076-foot low point, which conflicts with the trailhead at 7,709 (DEM) / 7,723 (Forest Service) — the logged segment probably starts above the trailhead. Camp elevation (~8,600 ft) is interpolated, not sourced, and is marked as such on the profile.
The Wigwam Park coordinate is an OpenStreetMap node on Wigwam Creek rather than a surveyed feature centre. Good enough to anchor the far end of the diagram; not a navigation target.

Corrected after first publication: this brief originally gave the South Park ranger district as the contact. Goose Creek trailhead is South Platte district — (303) 275-5610 — and the earlier number reaches the office for the Lost Park side of the wilderness. It also said no food-storage requirement existed; a forest-wide order in force to 2028 does require a 10-ft-up, 4-ft-out hang, and covers cookware and toiletries.

Fire restrictions are the one genuinely unresolved item. Stage 1 ran from March 27 to August 1, 2026; Stage 2 was signed June 29 and escalated it, and the forest's own alert page gave the Stage 2 order an August 1 end date as well. Whether anything is in force on August 17 is unknowable today — assume stove-only and call the district.

This brief prices Southwest deliberately. Frontier flies the same nonstop for $118, but its carry-on and checked-bag fees are published only as date-dependent ranges, so no honest total can be built from that fare — and a pack has to be checked.
Commons has no freely licensed photograph of the Shafthouse, Refrigerator Gulch, or Goose Creek itself; the one photo here shows granite formations elsewhere in the same wilderness.
